topic.label: Accounting
topic.desc: Recording and reporting money: bookkeeping and the general ledger, financial statements, GAAP and IFRS, audit, and management accounting.

concepts: Double-entry bookkeeping, chart of accounts, journal entries, reconciliation and closing the books.
Income statement, balance sheet, cash flow statement and how they link.
Accounting standards: US GAAP, IFRS, revenue recognition, leases and differences between them.
External audit, internal controls, SOX, materiality and audit evidence.
Budgets, cost allocation, unit economics and variance analysis for decisions.
skills: Builds double-entry journal entries for a transaction and checks debits equal credits.
Reconciles a bank statement to the ledger and lists unmatched items.
Shows how a transaction flows through the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement.
Reads a company's financial statements and summarizes profitability, liquidity and leverage.
Applies the five-step revenue recognition model to a contract.
Compares the GAAP and IFRS treatment of an item and its effect on reported numbers.
Finds gaps in internal controls over a financial process.
Explains budget versus actual variances by driver.
Computes contribution margin, CAC, LTV and payback for a business.
